item.title: Steenhuisen ‘seriously concerned’ about provisional liquidation application for Tongaat Hulett
item.description: John Steenhuisen, minister of agriculture, has now also voiced his serious concerns for the South African sugarcane value chain following recent news that the sugar milling giant, Tongaat Hulett, is likely to be placed under provisional liquidation.

item.title: Temperatures drop, but early frost unlikely
item.description: As the western parts of the country experienced extremely hot conditions over the past few days, weak cold fronts elsewhere caused minimum temperatures to drop to about 10°C. Farmers wondered whether the first frost of the year may be on its way.

item.title: WATCH | Cost of FMD vaccines – ‘Now is not the time to make a profit,’ says Steenhuisen
item.description: Farmers who want to vaccinate their herds against foot-and-mouth disease early, once enough doses are available in the country, will pay between R45 and R80 per animal, depending on the supplier. “We’ve been very clear with Onderstepoort Biological Products that we’re in a crisis and this is not an opportunity to make a profit.”

item.title: FMD | Political row erupts over KZN crisis response
item.description: The Democratic Alliance and KwaZulu-Natal’s provincial government are locked in a public dispute over the province’s response to the spread of foot-and-mouth disease (FMD).

item.title: WATCH | Sugar industry in crisis – KZN’s premier pushing to save Tongaat Hulett
item.description: One million livelihoods are now closer than ever to the brink of disaster unless all stakeholders – both private and state – in South Africa’s 178-year-old commercial sugarcane value chain urgently and constructively work together to address the multiple heavy, and potentially crippling, blows that just keep on coming.

item.title: FMD in Botswana: Thousands vaccinated, but export markets suspend meat imports
item.description: Botswana’s rapid response to recent outbreaks of foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) there has identified infections at multiple locations, resulting in thousands of cattle already being vaccinated. Important trade partners have also suspended their imports of products from animals that could carry the virus.

item.title: SA’s poultry sector overtakes US in global competitiveness rankings
item.description: South Africa has achieved a remarkable milestone in agricultural competitiveness, with its poultry sector now outperforming the United States and ranking second globally, trailing only Brazil, according to the newly released BFAP 2025 Competitiveness Benchmark Report.

item.title: Agriculture adds 30 000 more jobs to SA’s labour force in Q4 of 2025
item.description: Despite the challenges of foot-and-mouth disease facing livestock farmers across the country, agriculture has emerged as one of South Africa’s most dynamic employment sectors.
